title: Fixed-width integers and size_t
recap: The <cstdint> header provides fixed-width aliases such as std::int32_t when the implementation supports an integer of exactly that width. Use a fixed-width type when a guaranteed range or representation width is part of the requirement.

sizeof returns std::size_t, an implementation-defined unsigned integral type used for object byte sizes and lengths. Include <cstddef> when naming std::size_t explicitly, and avoid the often character-like 8-bit fixed-width aliases for ordinary numeric output.
objectives: Use std::int32_t for signed values requiring an exact 32-bit width.
Store a sizeof result in std::size_t with <cstddef> included.
Calculate a byte count from a field size and field count.
warnings: Fixed-width aliases are available only when the implementation has an exactly matching type.
std::int8_t and std::uint8_t commonly stream like character types.
std::size_t is unsigned and should not be mixed casually with signed arithmetic.
Do not assume the width of plain int when an exact 32-bit requirement is stated.
challenge: Repair a fixed packet summary. Exactly 48,000 packets were received and 49,200 were sent, so the signed packet delta is received minus sent. A payload contains 3 fields, each with the byte size of std::int32_t; calculate payloadBytes by multiplying fieldBytes by fieldCount rather than adding them. Report the field count and whether the payload calculation is correct instead of assuming a platform-specific byte count. Preserve the std::int32_t and std::size_t roles, use no input, and derive all output from the fixed objects.
hints: The sign of a delta depends on operand order: received minus sent is negative here.
Store sizeof(std::int32_t) in std::size_t, but do not assume how many bits the implementation places in one C++ byte.
A total for equally sized fields is fieldBytes multiplied by fieldCount.
